scope: Current-process/current-thread pseudo handles for process scheduling and affinity; owned native guest-thread handles additionally support thread priority as specified below. One unrestricted x86 guest group, up to 32 online native CPUs, consistent with SYSTEM_INFO. No external process/thread handles or strict CPU pinning.
qualification: A declared POSIX niceness mapping, not identical Windows scheduling or a performance guarantee. Only successful native setpriority calls report success. Permission failures map to ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. Realtime/background classes and strict thread affinity return ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED; no fake affinity state is stored.

thread_priority.scope: Owned native guest threads and current-thread pseudo handle. Validate supported Windows relative values -15,-2,-1,0,1,2,15; wait for real native thread registration before applying.
thread_priority.mapping: pthread_setschedparam(SCHED_OTHER): queried min/max for IDLE/TIME_CRITICAL, integer midpoint plus relative offset for other values, clamped to queried range.
thread_priority.qualification: Explicit Apple policy, not realtime scheduling or Windows priority equivalence. Return success only after native application; preserve permission and native errors. Finished or invalid thread handles fail.
thread_priority.validation: Component test queries the worker with pthread_getschedparam and verifies the requested native endpoint after successful SetThreadPriority.
